title: Weight shift under a Tate twist
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ and an isomorphism
$\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ as in
[def-weil-punctual-weights]. If a lisse
Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, then its
Tate twist $\mathcal F(n)$ is
punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w-2n$, for every
$n\in\mathbf Z$. The same shift holds for upper weight bounds: if
$\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$, then
$\mathcal F(n)$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w-2n$.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $b=q^{-n}\in\Qlb^\times$. Apply [lem-pur-twist-frobenius-scalar] with $\Lambda=\Qlb$ and twist index $n$: the Tate object on $s$ is concentrated in degree zero, its sections are one-dimensional, and its geometric Frobenius is $b$. By [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], choosing a nonzero generator of those sections identifies the underlying object with the coefficient unit on $s$: the map from the unit determined by that generator becomes an isomorphism under the fully faithful fibre functor. Pull this identification back along $Y\to s$. The comparison of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists] identifies this pullback with $\Qlb(n)_Y$. This identification respects the canonical Weil structures: in [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] these are built from the same functorial maps on roots of unity, followed by limits, tensor powers and duals. Consequently, in the chosen geometric trivialization, the Weil structure of the Tate line is $b$ times the coefficient-unit structure. This also covers negative $n$, since the cited scalar theorem already includes every integer twist.

source.place: first sentence: Frobenius-on-twists normalization; replace the definition-only scalar citation by its named theorem

proof.text: For any constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal G$, tensoring with the trivialized line of step 1 identifies the underlying object of $\mathcal G(n)$ with $\mathcal G$. The tensor formula for $\theta_{K(n)}$ in [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists] becomes $\theta_{\mathcal G(n)}=b\theta_{\mathcal G}$. The pullback-tensor comparison is natural and compatible with composition by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], so these identifications can be used in the iterated pullbacks defining the local operator. At a closed point $y$ of degree $m\geq1$, the definition [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] composes exactly $m$ copies of the Weil structure, with the same point transport on the unchanged underlying object. Pullback and transport are linear over the coefficient field; the scalar $b$ is therefore unchanged in each copy. Thus $F_y(\mathcal G(n))=b^m F_y(\mathcal G)=q^{-mn}F_y(\mathcal G)$ under this identification.

source.place: first sentence and parenthesis: local operator is the m-fold iterate; write the scalar iteration explicitly

proof.text: Write $c=q^{-mn}\ne0$ and $A=F_y(\mathcal G)$. An eigenvector $v\ne0$ of $A$ with eigenvalue $\alpha$ satisfies $(cA)v=(c\alpha)v$. Conversely $(cA)v=\beta v$ implies $Av=(c^{-1}\beta)v$. Hence the eigenvalues after twisting are exactly the $c\alpha$. This uses the eigenvector definition recalled in [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights] and does not assume that $A$ is semisimple.

source.place: second sentence: eigenvalue scaling, in both directions

proof.text:
Suppose $\mathcal G$ is punctually pure of real weight $u$. At $y$ the definition [def-weil-punctual-weights] gives $|\iota(\alpha)|=q_y^{u/2}$. As a finite extension of $k_0$ of degree $m$, $\kappa(y)$ has $q^m$ elements: a vector-space basis identifies its underlying set with $k_0^m$. Thus $q_y=q^m$. A field isomorphism fixes rational numbers, so $\iota(q^{-mn})=q^{-mn}>0$. Multiplicativity of the complex absolute value [def-weil-complex-absolute-value] and the power laws [def-weil-real-power] give
$$|\iota(q^{-mn}\alpha)|=q^{-mn}q_y^{u/2}=q_y^{-n}q_y^{u/2}=q_y^{(u-2n)/2}.$$
Together with step 3 this is precisely punctual purity of weight $u-2n$. Take $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$ and $u=w$ for the first assertion. Steps 1--4 required only constructibility, so the same argument applies to constructible graded pieces below.

source.place: displayed absolute-value equality and its interpretation as punctual purity

proof.text:
For the mixed assertion, choose the finite filtration $0=\mathcal F_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal F_r=\mathcal F$ and real weights $u_j\leq w$ from [def-weil-punctual-weights]. In the trivialization of step 1, twisting keeps every underlying sheaf and every morphism unchanged and multiplies each Weil structure by the same invertible scalar $b$. Thus each inclusion is still a Weil morphism, since multiplying both sides of $i\theta=\theta' g^*i$ by $b$ preserves that equation. Kernels and quotients, including their underlying constructible objects, are unchanged; their induced Weil structures are multiplied by $b$ as well. In particular
$\mathcal F_j(n)/\mathcal F_{j-1}(n)\cong(\mathcal F_j/\mathcal F_{j-1})(n)$ as Weil sheaves. This proves the needed exactness directly, rather than inferring a sheaf filtration from stalk-module mixedness. By step 4 every displayed quotient is punctually pure of weight $u_j-2n\leq w-2n$. The same finite filtration, now with these shifted weights, witnesses mixedness of $\mathcal F(n)$ by the cited definition. The empty filtration for the zero sheaf is included.

source.place: last sentence: exactness on the sheaf filtration, graded-piece purity, and the upper bound

proof_origin.place: entire proof, with the scalar theorem and the sheaf-filtration argument made explicit; checked against Deligne Weil II (1.2.5)(iv), (1.2.6), (1.2.7), pp. 154-155
